scenes.text: You can't tickle yourself, because your brain sees it coming.
A part at the back of your brain, the cerebellum, predicts what your own movements will feel like.
Then it turns down the feeling before it even arrives.
Scientists at University College London tested this with a tickling robot.
When people moved the robot themselves, adding a tiny delay made the tickle feel stronger.
The less your brain can predict a touch, the more it tickles.
Are you super ticklish, or not at all?

title: Why you can't tickle yourself 🤭
caption: Your cerebellum predicts the touch from your own movements and dampens it, so self-tickling feels weak. UCL researchers found that adding a small delay with a robot made it feel more ticklish! 🤭
